steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Dramatic irony: audience knows something characters don't — creates tension, humour or foreboding. | Key Fact: Soliloquy: character alone on stage speaking thoughts — reveals inner truth to audience. | Key Fact: Aside: character briefly shares thoughts with audience — conspiratorial, breaks fourth wall. | Key Fact: Cross-cutting: switching between two scenes — creates contrast, parallel or tension.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe three dramatic devices a playwright might use to reveal a character's true thoughts to the audience. | How does dramatic irony create tension in a play you have studied? | Explain how cross-cutting and juxtaposition can be used to highlight a play's themes.
